title: Measuring the Part of a Protection Plan's Term Still to Come
content:
The part of a Pass and Trip Protection plan's term still to come, on which the return of premium is taken, is
measured in one of three ways.

1. Where the plan's premium is collected alongside the covered holding's instalments and instalments still
   fall on its schedule, the part still to come is the days from the day the plan is treated as given up from
   to the day cover is due to end, as a share of the days from the day cover began to the day cover is due to
   end.
2. Where the plan's premium is collected in a single payment, the part still to come is the whole months still
   to come as a share of the whole months from the day cover began to the day cover is due to end.
3. In every other case the part still to come is the instalments still to fall on the covered holding's
   schedule as a share of all the instalments that schedule holds.

**Where the schedule is read from.** Whether instalments still fall, and how many the schedule holds
altogether, are read from the covered holding's own tier and account under the Season Pass Programme: the
number of instalments that holding's tier holds, against the entries its account shows charging an instalment
within the season.

**Worked cases (hypothetical inputs).** A plan riding on the covered holding's instalments, that schedule
holding 6 instalments of which 2 have been charged, cover running 180 days from the day it began to the day it
is due to end and the plan treated as given up with 45 of those days still to come: the part still to come is
45 days over 180 days, which is a quarter. A plan collected in a single payment, cover running 5 whole months
with 2 whole months still to come: the part still to come is 2 months over 5 months, which is two fifths. A
plan riding on a schedule on which no instalment still falls, that schedule holding 6: the part still to come
is nothing over 6, which is nothing.
